set: B: one sheet of each acting state the page uses, confident, nervous, plain, scared, angry, shocked and exhausted, with no time and no word on it

issues.where: Frames 2–7, pause beside the first two fields
issues.what: The unchanged stock cursor stance gives the pause duration but almost no readable response to the transition or anticipation before the dash.
issues.fix: Give the transition a short recoil, then hold a visibly loaded lean or compression just before the stretched launch.

issues.where: Frames 5–10, between the fields and at the rotary dial reveal
issues.what: The arrow mostly changes angle and position. There is a small compression at the field, but no held reaction that separates discovering the dial from simply navigating to it.
issues.fix: Add a readable checked pose as the dial is revealed, then load the tail and release into the existing dash.

issues.where: Frames 5–9, between the incoming lines of text
issues.what: A brief bend signals unease, but it resolves to a near-stock cursor before the feeling registers clearly; the text motion carries more of the beat than the arrow does.
issues.fix: Hold the bent, braced posture a little longer and let the tip turn toward the new line before settling or leaving.

issues.what: The burst gets a crisp initial flinch, but the long departure reads as an ordinary pointer glide once the coins are out of view. The startled state drops away without a visible recovery.
issues.fix: Add a compact overshoot or shudder on stopping and hold a distinct recovering pose before returning to neutral.

issues.where: Frames 9–12, crossing the orange crank handle
issues.what: The handle partly covers the arrow, but its body does not clearly dodge, squash or snap back through the crossing. The flame reads immediately; the arrow's response to the moving handle does not.
issues.fix: Stage a clear recoil or compression on one side of the handle, with a readable arrow silhouette and a brief aftermath pose.

reads.read: Wary or briefly stunned after a bright scene change, it pauses beside two fields, then commits and darts between them.
Curious and tentative, it noses between two fields, activates one, then lunges for the rotary telephone dial that appears and starts dialing.
Alert, then uneasy or puzzled as lines of text appear around it; it cringes briefly, hesitates, then moves toward the fields.
Startled when the date-of-birth slot machine spits out coins; it flinches toward the lever, then bolts away and settles.
It leaves the volume crank and rushes toward Continue, then stalls in a drooping, frustrated crouch when the gauge drains; it perks up as the bars begin lighting again.
Alarmed and urgent as its tip catches fire, it shoots back across the rising volume gauge toward the still-spinning crank, where the handle sweeps into its path.
Spent and lifeless: the smoking arrow goes out and collapses into a crumpled shell, then hangs limp as the crank panel slides out of view.
